Package io.webagent4j.recording.replay

Enum Class ReplayFailureType

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<ReplayFailureType>
io.webagent4j.recording.replay.ReplayFailureType
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<ReplayFailureType>, Constable
public enum ReplayFailureType extends Enum<ReplayFailureType>
A structured, secret-free reason Deterministic Replay could not proceed.

This enum currently covers only the failure categories the structural/decision replay scope implemented so far can actually produce - see docs/recording.md for the full taxonomy the broader Deterministic Replay design anticipates (including categories specific to real governed-target side-effect replay, such as a target revalidation failure, an action execution failure, a missing replay input, or a secret mismatch) and why that scope is not yet implemented. Constants are added here only once code exists that can produce them - this module does not define a failure category for a feature that does not yet exist.

There is deliberately no constant here for an internally inconsistent recording (a tree that does not correspond to its own plan) - not because that check does not exist, but because it can never run at replay time in the first place: WorkflowRecordingV2's own compact constructor (see RecordingV2PlanTreeValidator) already rejects such a recording before an instance can exist, so ReplayValidator and WorkflowReplayer can never receive one to classify with a replay-time failure type.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • INCOMPATIBLE_WORKFLOW

      public static final ReplayFailureType INCOMPATIBLE_WORKFLOW
      The recording's own WorkflowExecutionPlan is not identical to the live workflow's current plan (WorkflowPlanner.plan(workflow)): the workflow definition has changed, or workflow is simply a different workflow, since this recording was captured. A recording is never replayed against a workflow it does not structurally match.

    • UNSUPPORTED_STATUS

      public static final ReplayFailureType UNSUPPORTED_STATUS
      The recording's overall WorkflowStatus is not one this replay scope supports. Only a COMPLETED recording is replayable in this scope: replaying a FAILED trace raises its own semantics questions (chiefly, what "replaying" a failure that was often itself action-related would even mean without real side effects) that this scope deliberately leaves undecided rather than guess at - see WorkflowRecordingV2 and Workflow.

    • LOOP_ITERATION_COUNT_EXCEEDS_BOUND

      public static final ReplayFailureType LOOP_ITERATION_COUNT_EXCEEDS_BOUND
      A recorded WorkflowStepType.LOOP's number of actually-run iterations exceeds the live workflow's own declared maxIterations for that step - added in 1.3.0. A recording's own structural plan never encodes maxIterations (see docs/workflow.md#bounded-loops), so this check is made here, against the live Workflow, rather than as part of WorkflowRecordingV2's own construction-time invariants: a hostile recording claiming to be a genuine, COMPLETED trace of a bounded loop cannot smuggle in more iterations than that loop's live definition actually authorizes, even though the recording's plan and tree are otherwise perfectly self-consistent.
